fields.description:
## Context / Problem

Rebar has measured mutation evidence for seven behavioral cores, but Gerrit does not detect
when a changed test weakens those contracts. Mutmut changes production code, so changed tests
must select the production shard they cover. The blocking lane stays targeted; a weekly/manual
all-shard sweep detects mapping and tool drift.

## Approach

Use the targeted, pinned pattern seen in active OSS workflows, adapted to rebar's Gerrit
`Verified` authority. `.github/mutation-shards.toml` is the sole source for each
shard's production selector, test/support inputs, normalized equivalent-mutant fingerprints,
and numeric budgets. The driver generates the effective per-shard mutmut configuration and a
human-readable summary from that manifest; `pyproject.toml` and the documentation do not carry
independent shard lists or budget values.

The driver diffs the commit against its single parent, including both sides of renames. A mapped
source, test, or support change selects its shard;
mutation driver/config/lock changes select all shards. Changed files under `tests/` that match no
protected shard are reported as advisory mapping gaps. An unresolved parent/diff fails closed;
an empty selection is a successful, explicit skip.

Each shard runs from fresh base/head archives with no restored `mutants/` verdict state.
Dependency caching is allowed. Python 3.12, `mutmut==3.7.0`,
`--max-children 1`, mutmut's `(clean-test duration + 1 second) x 15` timeout, and a 30-minute job
limit bound the run. Selected clean tests run before mutation.

Comparison is per mutation unit (module + qualified function). When its source bytes are
identical at base and head, every base killed mutant must still exist and be killed at head; this
also applies to unchanged functions in mixed patches. Unmatched base/head units are explicitly
reported as source-changed and use head budgets, never silently dropped: `foo` renamed to `bar`
reports one removed plus one added unit, then validates every `bar` outcome. Changed units use
head budgets because valid edits can add or renumber mutants; exact-ID deltas are advisory. A survivor is
accepted only when the normalized `mutmut show` diff
(location headers removed) matches a manifest fingerprint and the shard remains within its
survivor ceiling. Zero mutants, unknown statuses/fingerprints, or budget failures block.

Allowed head outcomes are killed mutants, fingerprinted equivalent survivors within budget,
and `no tests` results within their separate historical ceiling. Timeout ceilings are zero.
`not checked`, interrupted, suspicious, skipped, segfault, caught-by-type-check, and unknown
statuses fail because this gate does not enable type-check filtering and cannot prove those
mutants were exercised. Mapped score is `killed / (killed + survived + timeout)`.

On failure, head non-killed mutants rerun once to classify regressions versus nondeterminism;
either stays red. Only independently identified dependency-install/setup
failures may retry. Results and raw outputs are always published, and newer patchsets cancel
older runs.

The Gerrit implementation is explicit: `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` invokes a targeted
`mutation` job on the exact patchset and lists it in `vote.needs`.
`.github/workflows/test.yml` has the push/PR mirror job required by the source-lane parity contract
at `scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py:44-58`; the broad workflow reuses the driver and manifest.
This matches vote aggregation at `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml:310-317`.

Historical ceilings from `docs/mutation-testing.md:98-122` are:

| Shard | Survivors max | No-tests max | Timeouts max | Score floor |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| signing | 3 | 110 | 0 | 99.2% |
| reducer processors | 5 | 0 | 0 | 99.4% |
| next batch | 6 | 208 | 0 | 99.2% |
| gates | 0 | 376 | 0 | 100.0% |
| validate | 0 | 223 | 0 | 100.0% |
| compact policy | 0 | 0 | 0 | 100.0% |
| push policy | 0 | 0 | 0 | 100.0% |

A budget may change only with the affected source or mapping, measured base/head results, and
an updated rationale. A budget-only relaxation fails validation.

## Scope

- `.github/mutation-shards.toml`, `scripts/mutation_gate.py`: canonical shard data, selection,
  clean base/head execution, comparison, fingerprints, and failure classification.
- `.github/workflows/_mutation.yml`, `.github/workflows/mutation.yml`: reusable targeted runner
  and weekly/manual all-shard sweep.
- `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`, `.github/workflows/test.yml`: exact-patchset Gerrit job,
  `vote.needs`, and its push/PR mirror counterpart.
- `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`: pin mutmut 3.7.0 and remove the duplicate global shard selection;
  the driver writes effective per-shard config into each fresh archive.
- `docs/mutation-testing.md`: explain cadence, manifest authority, fingerprint/no-tests rationale,
  unmatched tests, and budget-change policy without duplicating manifest values.
- `tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py`, `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py`: hermetic driver
  behavior and workflow/vote parity.

## Testing

Hermetic tests cover selection including renames/deletions, unmatched tests, manifest validation,
mixed patches, statuses, fingerprints, budgets, failures, reruns, artifacts, and vote aggregation.
A real mutmut 3.7.0 smoke run executes compact-policy from fresh base/head archives.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Selection tests prove mapped source/test/support changes choose only the specified shards.
- [ ] Selection tests prove infrastructure changes choose every shard.
- [ ] Diff-edge tests prove renames/deletions are mapped, unmatched tests are advisory, empty
  selection is explicit, unresolved parent/diff is red.
- [ ] Fresh-archive tests prove base/head runs restore no mutation verdict state.
- [ ] Execution tests prove the pinned runtime/concurrency/timeouts, clean-test preflight, plus
  zero-mutant rejection.
- [ ] Comparison tests prove identical mutation units block missing or killed-to-non-killed base
  mutants, including unchanged functions in mixed patches.
- [ ] Comparison tests prove unmatched base/head units are reported as source-changed plus checked
  against head budgets.
- [ ] Changed-unit tests prove exact-ID deltas are advisory while unknown statuses/fingerprints or
  survivor/no-tests/timeout/score budget failures block.
- [ ] Retry-policy tests prove only setup may retry; mutation reruns remain red.
- [ ] Reporting tests distinguish skip/mapping gap, baseline test, setup/tool, timeout, regression,
  nondeterminism; raw artifacts publish for every outcome.
- [ ] Workflow tests prove the targeted job exists in Gerrit plus the push/PR mirror, appears in
  `vote.needs`, passes `python scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py`.
- [ ] Workflow tests prove newer patchsets cancel older runs.
- [ ] Driver-equivalence tests prove targeted plus broad modes read the same manifest and budgets.
- [ ] Artifact tests prove targeted plus broad modes publish the same result format.
- [ ] A real compact-policy smoke run with mutmut 3.7.0 passes from fresh base/head archives.
- [ ] Documentation names the manifest as authoritative.
- [ ] Documentation explains cadence, fingerprints, no-tests allowances, mapping gaps, plus the
  measured budget-change rule.

## Verification

    pytest -q tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py
    python scripts/mutation_gate.py smoke --shard compact-policy --base HEAD^ --head HEAD
    python scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py
    make lint
    make typecheck

## Primary evidence

Mutmut 3.7.0: https://github.com/boxed/mutmut/tree/3.7.0. A 2026-08-10 ticket-comment probe records
the observed CLI, IDs, status map, timeout fields, `show` diff, and CI-stat omissions. Earlier
research comments cite current Instructor, DataDog, PostHog, Trailmark, and GeoParquet workflows.
